source.title: Pure O-sequences: known results, applications, and open problems

accepted.question_text: A pure O-sequence is the degree-count vector h = (h0 = 1, h1, ..., he) of a pure monomial order ideal, where all maximal monomials have the same degree e, and its type is the number of maximal monomials. Determine the largest type t for which every pure O-sequence, across all codimensions and socle degrees, must be unimodal.

evidence.quote: A monomial order ideal, X, is called pure if all maximal monomials of X (in the partial ordering given by divisibility) have the same degree. A pure O-sequence is the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal. ... The type of a pure O-sequence is the number of maximal monomials.

1. What is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal (indepenﬀdently of the codimension or socle degree)? Even proving that t ≥ 2, i.e., that pure O-sequences of type 2 are unimodal in any codimension, would be very interesting.

accepted.question_text: For a fixed codimension r, where codimension is the number of variables of the underlying monomial algebra, determine the largest type t such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r is unimodal.

evidence.quote: We will usually be a monomial ideal. Without loss of generality we will assume that I does not contain nonzero linear forms, so we will define r to be the codimension of A.
2. For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest type t for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed codimension r, determine the largest socle degree e such that every pure O-sequence of codimension r and socle degree e is unimodal.

evidence.quote: Thus the study of pure O-sequences boils down to a study of the possible Hilbert functions of artinian monomial level algebras.
3. For a fixed codimension r, what is the largest socle degree e for which all pure O-sequences are unimodal?

accepted.question_text: Determine the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4.

evidence.quote: A natural question, then, is what is the smallest codimension for which nonunimodal pure O-sequences exist with socle degree 4. This remains open.
4. What is the smallest codimension r for which there exists a nonunimodal pure O-sequence of socle degree 4?

accepted.question_text: Let P(*, e, t) denote the set of pure O-sequences with socle degree e and type t. For fixed e and large t, determine the asymptotic behavior and order of magnitude of the counting function #P(*, e, t).

evidence.quote: Fix positive integers e and t. Since the number of monomials dividing t monomials of degree e is finite, there are only finitely many pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t. Denote their set by P(∗, e, t).
5. Determine asymptotically the number #P(∗, e, t) of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t, for t large. What is the order of magnitude of #P(∗, e, t)?

accepted.question_text: A pure f-vector is the rank vector of a pure simplicial complex, equivalently a pure O-sequence generated by squarefree monomials. Stanley's first nonunimodal example was the Cohen-Macaulay simplicial-complex f-vector (1, n = 505, 2065, 3395, 3325, 3493). Determine the smallest number of variables n, equivalently the smallest number of vertices of a pure simplicial complex, for which a nonunimodal pure f-vector exists.

evidence.quote: In particular, if we define as pure those simplicial complexes whose facets have all the same dimension, then clearly their rank vectors, called pure f-vectors, are the special subset of pure O-sequences that can be generated by squarefree monomials.

6. The first example of a nonunimodal pure O-sequence (due to Stanley [66], 1977) was (1, n = 505, 2065, 3395, 3325, 3493), which is in fact the f-vector of a Cohen�ateaulay simplicial complex, hence in particular a pure f-vector. What is the
smallest number of variables n (i.e., the number of vertices of the complex) allowing the existence of a nonunimodal pure f-vector?

accepted.question_text: For matroid complexes, determine whether every matroid f-vector is unimodal or even log-concave, and determine whether every matroid h-vector is unimodal or log-concave. Here a matroid h-vector is the h-vector of the Stanley-Reisner ring of a matroid complex, and Stanley's conjecture predicts that every matroid h-vector is a pure O-sequence.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.4. Any matroid h-vector is a pure O-sequence.

7. Stanley’s Twenty-Fifth Problem for the year 2000 IMU Volume “Mathematics: frontiers and perspectives” [70] asks, among a few other things: are all matroid f-vectors unimodal, or even log-concave? What about matroid h-vectors?
